title: Docker
summary: Install Docker and learn every everyday command with its flags.

sections.title: Install
sections.lead: Pick your system. After installing, run the check command.

tabs.label: Windows
tabs.note: Needs Windows 10/11 with WSL 2. Docker Desktop sets it up for you.
tabs.more: Restart, open Docker Desktop, and wait for the whale icon to turn steady.

tabs.label: macOS
tabs.note: Works on Intel and Apple Silicon.
tabs.more: Or download Docker Desktop from docker.com and open it once to finish setup.

tabs.label: Ubuntu / Debian
commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y ca-certificates curl
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu $(. /etc/os-release && echo $VERSION_CODENAME) stable" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin
tabs.more: On Debian, replace 'ubuntu' with 'debian' in both URLs.

tabs.label: Any Linux
tabs.note: Convenience script. Fine for learning, not for production servers.

sections.title: Basics
sections.lead: Four words cover most of Docker.

items: A read-only template: your app plus everything it needs. Like a recipe.
A running copy of an image. Like a dish made from the recipe.
A folder outside the container so data survives when it is deleted.
A place to store and download images. Docker Hub is the default.

blocks.text: Flow: write a Dockerfile, build an image, run a container, push the image to a registry.

sections.title: Containers
sections.lead: Create, run, inspect and stop containers.

blocks.name: docker run
blocks.what: Create and start a container from an image.
options: Map host port 8080 to container port 80
Delete the container when it stops

blocks.name: docker ps
blocks.what: List containers.

blocks.name: docker stop / start / restart
blocks.what: Stop, start or restart a container by name or ID.
options: Seconds to wait before force kill (stop)
blocks.example: docker stop web && docker start web

blocks.name: docker rm
blocks.what: Delete a container.

blocks.name: docker logs
blocks.what: Show the output of a container.

blocks.name: docker exec
blocks.what: Run a command inside a running container.

blocks.name: docker inspect
blocks.what: Show full details (IP, mounts, config) as JSON.
options: Pick one field with a Go template

blocks.name: docker cp
blocks.what: Copy files between host and container.
options: Use this form for the container side

blocks.name: docker stats
blocks.what: Live CPU and memory use.

sections.title: Images
sections.lead: Download, build, tag and clean up images.

blocks.name: docker build
blocks.what: Build an image from a Dockerfile.

blocks.name: docker images
blocks.what: List local images.

blocks.name: docker pull
blocks.what: Download an image from a registry.

blocks.name: docker push
blocks.what: Upload an image to a registry. Run docker login first.

blocks.name: docker tag
blocks.what: Add another name to an image.

blocks.name: docker rmi
blocks.what: Delete an image.

blocks.name: docker history
blocks.what: Show the layers of an image.

sections.title: Volumes & Networks
sections.lead: Keep data safe and let containers talk to each other.

blocks.name: docker volume create
blocks.what: Make a named volume.

blocks.name: docker volume ls / rm / inspect
blocks.what: List, delete or inspect volumes.

blocks.name: docker network create
blocks.what: Make a network. Containers on the same custom network reach each other by name.

blocks.name: docker network ls / connect / rm
blocks.what: List networks, attach a container, or delete a network.

sections.title: Compose
sections.lead: Run several containers from one docker-compose.yml file.

blocks.name: docker compose up
blocks.what: Create and start everything in the file.

blocks.name: docker compose down
blocks.what: Stop and remove containers and networks.

blocks.name: docker compose ps / logs
blocks.what: See service status or output.

blocks.name: docker compose exec
blocks.what: Run a command inside a service.
blocks.example: docker compose exec db psql -U postgres

blocks.title: Full docker-compose.yml example
blocks.code:
services:
  web:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8080:80"
    environment:
      - DB_HOST=db
    depends_on: [db]
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
    volumes:
      - dbdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
volumes:
  dbdata:

sections.title: Dockerfile
sections.lead: The instructions that describe how to build your image.

blocks.name: FROM
blocks.what: Base image to start from. Always the first line.

blocks.name: WORKDIR
blocks.what: Folder where the next commands run.

blocks.name: COPY
blocks.what: Copy files from your project into the image.

blocks.name: RUN
blocks.what: Run a command while building, like installing packages.

blocks.name: ENV
blocks.what: Set an environment variable.

blocks.name: EXPOSE
blocks.what: Document which port the app uses.

blocks.name: CMD / ENTRYPOINT
blocks.what: Command that runs when the container starts. CMD can be overridden, ENTRYPOINT is fixed.

blocks.title: Full Dockerfile example
blocks.code:
FROM node:20-alpine
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm install
COPY . .
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

sections.title: Clean up & Registry
sections.lead: Free disk space and log in to registries.

blocks.name: docker system df
blocks.what: See how much space Docker uses.

blocks.name: docker system prune
blocks.what: Remove stopped containers, unused networks and dangling images.

blocks.name: docker login / logout
blocks.what: Sign in to Docker Hub or another registry.

blocks.name: docker search
blocks.what: Search Docker Hub.
